stratum_policy: No Stage 3B task is assigned S1, S2, RC or Q. Strata are assigned by a later, versioned review of Arm-A calibration data; thresholds are the preregistered ones.

tasks.title: Brown-Forsythe screening, then classical or Welch one-way ANOVA with matching follow-ups
tasks.source_relation: adapted: fixed analysis plan, function-style contract, closed-form oracle
tasks.difficulty_hypothesis: Agents reach for car::leveneTest (not installed) or mean-centred Levene, apply pooled Tukey after a Welch omnibus, or forget that Welch's denominator df is fractional and that the pairwise branch must be unpooled with Holm.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The decision rule and every formula are given in the prompt; the work is implementation of base-R statistics. MCP package documentation does not change the answer.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Exact definitions of Welch's F and Tukey-Kramer p-values, and which base functions expose them (oneway.test, TukeyHSD, pairwise.t.test).
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes: stats help pages are installed locally
alternative_solution_paths: oneway.test + TukeyHSD + manual unpooled t tests
pairwise.t.test(pool.sd = FALSE) for the Welch branch

calibration_risks.ceiling: moderate: the plan is explicit and the building blocks are standard

pinned_evidence.oracle: closed-form Brown-Forsythe F, Welch F with weights n/s^2, Tukey-Kramer via ptukey; cross-checked at load against oneway.test, TukeyHSD and pairwise.t.test

scorer.contract: solution.R functions; hidden checks; passed/total; fully_correct

pool.stratum_if_calibrated: S2-like control (tool-use tax); can never become S1

tasks.title: Balanced two-way factorial ANOVA with interaction-aware simple-effects reporting
tasks.source_relation: adapted: fixed reporting rule, simple effects against the full-model MSE, closed-form oracle
tasks.difficulty_hypothesis: Agents report main effects in the presence of a crossover interaction, or compute simple effects from separate per-site ANOVAs (different error term and df) instead of the full-model residual mean square, or fail to stop on unbalanced data where the table is not uniquely defined.

mcp_relevance.rationale: Pure factorial-design reasoning with an explicit reporting rule; nothing depends on a package, version or documentation fact beyond base R.
mcp_relevance.information_need: How simple effects are tested against the pooled full-model error term.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes: textbook formulas and installed stats help
alternative_solution_paths: lm + anova for the table, then per-site SS from cell means with the full MSE
nested model comparison score ~ site vs score ~ site + site:treatment, split by site

calibration_risks.ceiling: moderate-high: a standard textbook procedure with explicit instructions

pinned_evidence.oracle: balanced-design closed-form sums of squares; cross-checked at load against anova(lm) and the nested-model identity SS(simple effects) = SS(A) + SS(AB)

scorer.contract: solution.R functions; hidden checks; passed/total; fully_correct

pool.stratum_if_calibrated: S2-like control (tool-use tax); can never become S1

tasks.title: Equal-weight marginal (Type III) tests in an unbalanced two-factor design
tasks.source_relation: adapted: new fixtures, function-style contract, independent cell-means oracle
tasks.difficulty_hypothesis: The default aov/anova table is sequential (Type I) and silently answers different hypotheses in an unbalanced design; drop1() on a default treatment-coded fit answers yet another question when an interaction is present; ordered factors switch to polynomial contrasts; and car::Anova, the usual shortcut, is not installed.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The task is statistical reasoning about hypotheses and contrast coding. The decisive facts (how contr.sum, drop1 scope and sequential SS behave) are in base R documentation that is also installed locally; no package version or ecosystem fact changes the answer.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Which linear hypotheses Type I/II/III sums of squares test, and how to obtain Type III values with base R only.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes: stats help pages (?drop1, ?contrasts, ?anova.lm) and the model-matrix algebra are available locally and in model knowledge
alternative_solution_paths: drop1(fit, scope = ~ ., test = 'F') on a contr.sum fit
explicit comparison of nested models built from effect-coded model matrices
cell-means linear-hypothesis (Wald/F) tests with equal-weight averaging

shared_features: Type I versus Type III hypotheses

calibration_risks.ceiling: moderate: strong models know the car::Anova idiom and the contr.sum + drop1 recipe
calibration_risks.floor: low: the output contract is fully specified

pinned_evidence.oracle: cell-means linear hypotheses L m = 0 with Var(m) = sigma^2 diag(1/n); self-checked against balanced anova() and against sequential SS at load time

scorer.contract: solution.R functions; hidden checks; passed/total; fully_correct

pool.stratum_if_calibrated: S2-like control (tool-use tax); can never become S1
blockers: scorer validation gate not passed on the current files

tasks.title: One-factor repeated-measures ANOVA with a Greenhouse-Geisser sphericity rule
tasks.source_relation: adapted: fixed epsilon rule, function-style contract, covariance-formula oracle
tasks.difficulty_hypothesis: Agents either treat repeated measurements as independent, rely on ez/afex (not installed) for the sphericity correction, apply the correction to the F statistic or only to one df, mix up Greenhouse-Geisser with Huynh-Feldt, or fail to drop subjects with a missing occasion.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The statistics are specified in the prompt; the only ecosystem fact is that the usual convenience packages (ez, afex, rstatix) are not installed, which the supplied lockfile shows directly.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Box's epsilon formula and the aov Error() decomposition for within-subject designs.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes: stats::aov help and textbook formulas
alternative_solution_paths: aov with Error(subject/time) plus epsilon from the double-centred covariance eigenvalues
subjects-by-occasions matrix with closed-form sums of squares
nlme::gls/lme with an unstructured covariance is NOT equivalent and does not satisfy the contract

calibration_risks.ceiling: low-moderate: epsilon computation is a known stumbling block
calibration_risks.floor: moderate: several exact numbers must all be right

pinned_evidence.oracle: subjects-by-occasions sums of squares and Box's epsilon; cross-checked at load against aov(Error()) and the eigenvalue form of epsilon

scorer.contract: solution.R functions; hidden checks; passed/total; fully_correct

pool.stratum_if_calibrated: S2-like control (tool-use tax); can never become S1

tasks.title: ANCOVA with a slope-homogeneity decision rule and covariate-adjusted means
tasks.source_relation: adapted: explicit decision tree, function-style contract, normal-equation oracle
tasks.difficulty_hypothesis: Agents enter treatment before the covariate (unadjusted F), skip the slope test and always report parallel-slope adjusted effects, evaluate adjusted means at baseline = 0 or at group-specific baselines, or fail to switch to conditional means when slopes differ.

mcp_relevance.rationale: Model specification and covariate reasoning in base R; no package or version fact is needed.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Which F test adjusts for the covariate, and how to evaluate fitted means at fixed covariate values.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes: lm, anova and predict are documented locally
alternative_solution_paths: explicit design matrices with RSS differences
drop1 on the parallel model for the adjusted treatment F

shared_features: linear model with factor and covariate

calibration_risks.ceiling: moderate: a standard analysis with an explicit plan

pinned_evidence.oracle: normal-equation OLS from explicit design matrices; cross-checked at load against anova(lm), model comparison and predict()

tasks.title: Treatment-by-time interaction with missing visits: random-intercept model and ML likelihood-ratio test
tasks.source_relation: adapted: fixed model and test, function-style contract, independent profile-likelihood oracle
tasks.difficulty_hypothesis: Agents drop incomplete participants and run a classical repeated-measures ANOVA, compare REML fits with different fixed effects, ignore the clustering, reach for lme4 (not installed) instead of the installed nlme, or fit time as a numeric trend and get the wrong degrees of freedom.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The standard answer in the wild uses lme4::lmer, which is not installed. Choosing nlme::lme and its ML/REML and VarCorr conventions is an API-availability and documentation question that package metadata and function documentation can inform (check_package_version, get_function_docs). It is not decisive: the lockfile and library(nlme) are available locally.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Which mixed-model package is installed and how nlme::lme exposes ML log-likelihoods, variance components and method = 'ML'.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes, partly: renv.lock and library(nlme) show availability, and nlme help is installed; MCP mainly shortens the lookup
alternative_solution_paths: nlme::lme with method = 'ML' for both models
nlme::gls with corCompSymm (equivalent for non-negative intraclass correlation)
an explicit profile-likelihood implementation in base R

calibration_risks.ceiling: low-moderate: needs the right package and the ML-versus-REML distinction
calibration_risks.floor: moderate: the optimiser-level tolerance is 1e-4 and the output contract is long

pinned_evidence.oracle: explicit profile-likelihood random-intercept ML (no nlme); cross-checked at load against nlme::lme logLik and sigma

scorer.contract: solution.R functions; hidden checks; passed/total; fully_correct

pool.stratum_if_calibrated: RC-like: target by task text; enters S1 only if its Arm-A screen falls in [0.10, 0.90] over >= 3 trials
